premises: A continuous B2 matrix causes poor room-temperature ductility in RHEAs
Inverting to a continuous BCC matrix with discrete B2 precipitates improves room-temperature ductility while maintaining high yield strength at room and elevated temperature
A heat treatment of 1050 °C for 2 hours with controlled air cooling can achieve this microstructural inversion
